---
title: "04 - Post-process and drop outliers from plot-level carbon data"
output: html_document
---

**Purpose.** Loads the six covariate-joined carbon datasets (AGC, BGC and SOC
stock and change) and post-processes them for analysis: adds "unknown" (or,
for the SOC control category, "chrono") dummy columns for rows with no dummy
category, drops outliers in the response variable using Tukey IQR fences
(k = 1.5), drops rows with stand age of 0, and drops binary predictor columns
with only one unique non-NA value. Histograms of the response before and after
filtering are shown. The outputs are the final analysis datasets used by notebooks
06-11.

**Inputs.**

- `output/data/agc_by_plot_and_age_w_covars.xlsx` (03a)
- `output/data/bgc_by_plot_and_age_w_covars.xlsx` (03a)
- `output/data/soc_by_plot_and_age_w_covars.xlsx` (03a)
- `output/data/agc_change_by_plot_and_age_w_covars.xlsx` (03b)
- `output/data/bgc_change_by_plot_and_age_w_covars.xlsx` (03b)
- `output/data/soc_change_by_plot_and_age_w_covars.xlsx` (03b)

**Outputs.**

- `output/data/<c_data_name>_by_plot_and_age_w_covars_drop_outliers.xlsx`
  for each of `agc`, `bgc`, `soc`, `agc_change`, `bgc_change`, `soc_change`

```{r setup}

library(here)
library(tidyverse)
library(openxlsx)

```

Load the covariate-joined carbon datasets.
```{r load-data}

agc_df <- read.xlsx(here("output", "data", "agc_by_plot_and_age_w_covars.xlsx"))
agc_change_df <- read.xlsx(here("output", "data", "agc_change_by_plot_and_age_w_covars.xlsx"))
bgc_df <- read.xlsx(here("output", "data", "bgc_by_plot_and_age_w_covars.xlsx"))
bgc_change_df <- read.xlsx(here("output", "data", "bgc_change_by_plot_and_age_w_covars.xlsx"))
soc_df <- read.xlsx(here("output", "data", "soc_by_plot_and_age_w_covars.xlsx"))
soc_change_df <- read.xlsx(here("output", "data", "soc_change_by_plot_and_age_w_covars.xlsx"))

```


Options: the datasets to process.
```{r options}

c_data_names <- c('agc', 'bgc', 'soc', 'agc_change', 'bgc_change', 'soc_change')

```

Define the binary predictor variables and dummy-variable column prefixes.
```{r var-groups}

bin_vars <- c('pruning', 'weed_control', 'tillage', 'pest_control', 'burning', 
              'litter_management', 'fertilizer', 'irrigation', 'grazing',
              'n_fix_bin', 'myco_fungi_am', 'myco_fungi_ecm', 
              'freezing_exposed', 'resprout_after_fire')

# plus af_cat, prior_*, soil_tex_*, ctrl_*

dummy_var_prefs <- c('prior_', 'soil_tex_', 'ctrl_')


```


Add a dummy column flagging rows with no category for each dummy-variable group (`<prefix>unknown`, or `ctrl_chrono` for the SOC control category).
```{r unknown-dummies}

for (c_data_name in c_data_names) {
  for (dummy_var_pref in dummy_var_prefs) {
    my_c_data <- get(paste0(c_data_name, '_df'))
    if (any(grepl(dummy_var_pref, names(my_c_data)))) {
      my_c_data <- my_c_data %>%
        rowwise() %>%
        mutate(my_dummy_rowsum = sum(c_across(starts_with(dummy_var_pref) & where(is.numeric)), na.rm = TRUE))
      if (dummy_var_pref == 'ctrl_') { # for soc_change, no 'ctrl' means it was part of a chronosequence
        my_c_data <- my_c_data %>%
          rowwise() %>%
          mutate(!!sym(paste0(dummy_var_pref, 'chrono')) := ifelse(my_dummy_rowsum == 0, 1, NA)) %>%
          dplyr::select(-my_dummy_rowsum)
      } else {
        my_c_data <- my_c_data %>%
          rowwise() %>%
          mutate(!!sym(paste0(dummy_var_pref, 'unknown')) := ifelse(my_dummy_rowsum == 0, 1, NA)) %>%
          dplyr::select(-my_dummy_rowsum)
      }
      assign(paste0(c_data_name, '_df'), my_c_data)
    }
  }
}


```


Histograms of the response variable before filtering (`c_t_ha` for stocks, `c_t_ha_delta` for SOC stock, `c_t_ha_yr` for change).
```{r hist-before}

for (c_data_name in c_data_names) {
  if(grepl('change', c_data_name)) {
    var_name <- 'c_t_ha_yr'
  } else if (c_data_name == 'soc') {
    var_name <- 'c_t_ha_delta'
  } else {
    var_name <- 'c_t_ha'
  }
  
  plot_obj <- get(paste0(c_data_name, '_df')) %>%
    ggplot(aes(x = !!sym(var_name))) +
    geom_histogram(bins = 30, fill = "gray", color = "black", alpha = 0.8) +
    labs(title = c_data_name) +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 14)
  
  print(plot_obj)
}


```

Drop rows whose response value falls outside the Tukey IQR fences.

```{r drop-outliers}

# filter out values more than k * IQR beyond Q1/Q3 (Tukey-style fences)
# k = 1.5 is the conventional Tukey "outlier" fence; k = 1 was tried first to
# approximate the stringency of the previous 2-SD rule under normality, but
# empirically dropped 5-17% more rows than the 2-SD rule across datasets, so
# k = 1.5 was adopted instead as the more standard, less aggressive choice
# drop_rows argument specifies whether to drop the whole row, or just replace the outliers with NA
# lower fence is intentionally not clamped at 0, even for non-negative variables
toss_outliers_iqr <- function(c_data_name, var_name, drop_rows = T, k = 1.5) {
  
  df <- get(paste0(c_data_name, '_df'))
  
  # calculate IQR fences
  q1 <- quantile(df[[var_name]], 0.25, na.rm = T)
  q3 <- quantile(df[[var_name]], 0.75, na.rm = T)
  iqr_val <- q3 - q1
  low_lim <- q1 - k * iqr_val
  high_lim <- q3 + k * iqr_val
  
  print(paste0('Filtering out ', c_data_name, '$', var_name, ' outliers below ', low_lim, ' and above ', high_lim))
  
  
  if (drop_rows) {
    df_filt <- df %>%
      filter(
        !!sym(var_name) > low_lim,
        !!sym(var_name) < high_lim
      )
  } else {
    df_filt <- df %>%
      mutate(!!sym(var_name) := ifelse((!!sym(var_name) > low_lim) & 
                                         (!!sym(var_name) < high_lim),
                                       !!sym(var_name), NA))
  }
  
  return (df_filt)
}

for (c_data_name in c_data_names) {
  if(grepl('change', c_data_name)) {
    var_name <- 'c_t_ha_yr'
  } else if (c_data_name == 'soc') {
    var_name <- 'c_t_ha_delta'
  } else {
    var_name <- 'c_t_ha'
  }
  
  assign(paste0(c_data_name, '_df'), toss_outliers_iqr(c_data_name, var_name))
}

```

Drop rows with stand age of 0 (`age_mean` for change datasets, `age` for stock datasets).
```{r drop-age-0}

for (c_data_name in c_data_names) {
  if(grepl('change', c_data_name)) {
    age_var_name <- 'age_mean'
  } else {
    age_var_name <- 'age'
  }
  
  assign(paste0(c_data_name, '_df'), get(paste0(c_data_name, '_df')) %>%
           filter(!!sym(age_var_name) > 0))
}

```


Drop binary columns with only one unique non-NA value.
```{r drop-constant-bin}

for (c_data_name in c_data_names) {
  
  my_c_df <- get(paste0(c_data_name, '_df'))
  
  to_drop <- bin_vars[
    vapply(my_c_df[bin_vars],
           function(x) dplyr::n_distinct(x, na.rm = TRUE) <= 1,
           logical(1))
  ]
  
  print(paste0("Dropped binary columns with only one non-na value: ", c_data_name, ' - ', to_drop))
  
  my_c_df <- my_c_df %>%
    dplyr::select(-any_of(to_drop))
  
  assign(paste0(c_data_name, '_df'), my_c_df)
}

```


Histograms of the response variable after filtering.
```{r hist-after}

for (c_data_name in c_data_names) {
  if(grepl('change', c_data_name)) {
    var_name <- 'c_t_ha_yr'
  } else if (c_data_name == 'soc') {
    var_name <- 'c_t_ha_delta'
  } else {
    var_name <- 'c_t_ha'
  }
  
  plot_obj <- get(paste0(c_data_name, '_df')) %>%
    ggplot(aes(x = !!sym(var_name))) +
    geom_histogram(bins = 30, fill = "gray", color = "black", alpha = 0.8) +
    labs(title = c_data_name) +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 14)
  
  print(plot_obj)
}


```


Save the filtered datasets.
```{r save}

for (c_data_name in c_data_names) {
  write.xlsx(get(paste0(c_data_name, '_df')), 
             paste0(here("output", "data"), "/", c_data_name, '_by_plot_and_age_w_covars_drop_outliers.xlsx'))
}


```
